notes: retro runs a multi-agent retrospective ceremony: detect mode (feature/phase/sprint), spawn the relevant contributing role agents concurrently for phase-specific perspectives, then synthesize a 5-Why root-cause analysis, Lessons Learned per category, git velocity metrics, and prioritized Action Items into docs/retros/. Evaluate correct mode detection, concurrent agent spawn, and the synthesized report (Action Items presented to user).

evals.prompt: Now that the user-auth feature is delivered, run a retrospective on it.
evals.expected_output: Feature mode: spawns developer + code-review + unit-test + integration-test + ba agents concurrently (single message, background), synthesizes 5-Why on the top issues, Lessons Learned (Process/Design/Testing/Security), git metrics, and an Action Items table, writing docs/retros/RETRO-feature-user-auth-[date].md and presenting only the Action Items table.

evals.prompt: Do a sprint retrospective covering the last two weeks, 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-29.
evals.expected_output: Sprint mode over the given date range: spawns developer + code-review + unit-test + integration-test agents (skips ba-agent), collects git velocity/quality metrics for the range, and writes docs/retros/RETRO-sprint-[date].md with 5-Why, Lessons Learned, and prioritized Action Items.

evals.prompt: I'm stopping for the day mid-implementation — capture where we are so the next session can pick up.
evals.expected_output: Should route to handoff (a session-continuity document), not retro; retro is for a completed feature/phase/sprint review, and running it on in-progress work is an explicit anti-pattern.
